newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's PM says polls plan has enough support.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's PM says polls plan has enough support.

text.p: Turkey's Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said on Tuesday he had enough MPs behind him to win parliamentary backing for a plan to revamp his Islamist-led coalition and head for early elections.

"There is a majority in parliament. No-one should have any worries about that," Erbakan told a meeting of his Welfare Party MPs. He did not refer to widespread speculation he would resign on Wednesday and hand over power to his secularist deputy.

A rightist Turkish leader with a key position in parliament said on Monday he would back Erbakan's plans to hand power to coalition ally Tansu Ciller and go to the polls to clear up a row with the army over Islamist activism.

"We will say 'yes' to this alternative so as to put the ballot box in front of the nation. We will support it because we want stability in Turkey," Anatolian news agency quoted far-right leader Mushin Yazicioglu as saying late on Monday.
On paper, the government is short of the majority it needs to get the power transfer and any election legislation through parliament.
The coalition has 274 deputies in the 550-seat assembly. But far-right powerbroker Yazicioglu's Grand Unity Party has eight MPs, who could help the coalition over parliamentary hurdles.
President Suleyman Demirel, an avowed secularist, must also approve the power handover. He has not given any indications if he will allow the plan go go ahead.
